title: Tubby Hayes' sextet in Detroit; why his father left Detroit
summary: He works in Detroit with a six-piece band at River Rouge; an aside on the 1920s when his father was laid off in Detroit.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So I stayed with him until I got a job in Detroit working with a six-piece band. I think his name was Hayes, a tenor player -- Tubby, they called him. Not Tubby Hayes. This is Tubby we called him. And he had a guy named Johnny something who played piano, and Freddie Radcliff played the drums...
Freddie Radcliff. I remember him.
Yeah, he was in the band. Charles Johnson played alto saxophone. He was in the band. And I don't

know whether you heard of him, but he ended up in Buffalo. I think he went to Buffalo after he left...after the band broke up, you know. We stayed together for quite a while. We worked out in River Rouge.
River Rouge where the famous Ford plant...
Yeah. Well, we used to play out there every weekend, you know.
I guess Detroit and that whole area was always such a...
It was much better than most towns. At least they had work...
There were people working and they had money to spend.

That's right. But when I was there... When they first took me to Detroit, it wasn't shit happening there. I think that was back in 1927 or '29 or somewhere back there. My old man, he got laid off and he had to split.
That's why he went back to Oklahoma.

Yeah. Well, he had sense enough to do that. Because in Oklahoma he was all right, he did all right. He got ahold of some money and had a store, and put his brother in business, and told him that this was supposed to be mine -- which I never got. But I didn't...
You weren't supposed to do that anyway.
No, I wasn't supposed to have it no way. But anyway, that's some of the things that happen to you.
Anyway, here you are in Detroit working with this six-piece band.
Yeah.
Is this 1940?
Yeah, this is 1940. And I stayed with the band until I think almost up until '41.
